content: The soft palate, also known as the velum or muscular palate, is composed of soft tissue and forms the posterior portion of the roof of the mouth. Unlike the hard palate located at the anterior part of the mouth, the soft palate does not contain any bony structures. The soft palate is a movable structure made up of muscle fibers covered by a mucous membrane. It plays a critical role in closing off the nasal passages during the act of swallowing, preventing food or liquid from entering the nasal cavity. Additionally, the movement of the soft palate during breathing contributes to the production of the sound associated with snoring. When the soft palate is touched, it typically triggers a pronounced gag reflex in most individuals. This reflex is a protective mechanism to prevent foreign objects from entering the throat. The soft palate also has an essential function in speech. It separates the oral cavity (mouth) from the nasal cavity to produce oral speech sounds. If this separation is incomplete, air escapes through the nose during speech, resulting in a hypernasal quality to the voice. Images of the soft palate may include depictions of the soft palate without tonsils (post-tonsillectomy), the oral cavity, and sagittal sections showing the relationship between the nose, mouth, pharynx, and larynx. Some illustrations may also show the oral cavity with the cheeks transversely slit and the tongue pulled forward for anatomical clarity.
